title: Impact of Local Labor Demand Shocks on Wages

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
I'll use Instrumental Variables (IV) estimation with the Bartik shift-share instrument. The shift-share instrument leverages exogenous variation in national industry growth rates interacted with predetermined local industry composition to identify causal effects of local labor demand on wages. The key assumptions are: (1) national industry shocks are uncorrelated with unobserved local factors affecting wages (exclusion restriction), and (2) the instrument is relevant (strong first stage). This approach addresses endogeneity concerns where local wage changes might simultaneously affect labor demand.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load required libraries
library(AER)
library(stargazer)
library(lmtest)

# Read the data
data <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s83_data.csv")

# Display basic summary statistics
cat("Summary Statistics:\n")
print(summary(data))

# First Stage: Check instrument relevance
first_stage <- lm(x ~ z + controls, data = data)
cat("\n=== FIRST STAGE RESULTS ===\n")
print(summary(first_stage))

# F-statistic for instrument strength
f_stat <- summary(first_stage)$fstatistic[1]
cat(sprintf("\nFirst-stage F-statistic: %.3f\n", f_stat))
cat(sprintf("Instrument strength: %s\n", ifelse(f_stat > 10, "Strong", "Weak")))

# Reduced Form: Effect of instrument on outcome
reduced_form <- lm(y ~ z + controls, data = data)
cat("\n=== REDUCED FORM RESULTS ===\n")
print(summary(reduced_form))

# Second Stage: IV estimation
iv_model <- ivreg(y ~ x + controls | z + controls, data = data)
cat("\n=== IV (2SLS) RESULTS ===\n")
print(summary(iv_model))

# Extract key coefficient
iv_coef <- coef(iv_model)["x"]
iv_se <- sqrt(diag(vcov(iv_model)))["x"]
iv_tstat <- iv_coef / iv_se
iv_pvalue <- 2 * pt(-abs(iv_tstat), df = iv_model$df.residual)

cat(sprintf("\n=== MAIN RESULT ===\n"))
cat(sprintf("IV Estimate: %.4f\n", iv_coef))
cat(sprintf("Standard Error: %.4f\n", iv_se))
cat(sprintf("t-statistic: %.3f\n", iv_tstat))
cat(sprintf("p-value: %.4f\n", iv_pvalue))

# OLS for comparison
ols_model <- lm(y ~ x + controls, data = data)
cat("\n=== OLS COMPARISON ===\n")
ols_coef <- coef(ols_model)["x"]
cat(sprintf("OLS Estimate: %.4f\n", ols_coef))
cat(sprintf("IV Estimate: %.4f\n", iv_coef))
cat(sprintf("Difference (IV - OLS): %.4f\n", iv_coef - ols_coef))

# Robustness checks
cat("\n=== ROBUSTNESS CHECKS ===\n")

# 1. Test for weak instruments
weak_iv_test <- summary(first_stage)$fstatistic[1]
cat(sprintf("1. Weak IV test (F > 10): %s (F = %.3f)\n", 
           ifelse(weak_iv_test > 10, "PASS", "FAIL"), weak_iv_test))

# 2. Hausman test for endogeneity
hausman_test <- summary(iv_model, diagnostics = TRUE)
cat("2. Hausman test for endogeneity:\n")
print(hausman_test$diagnostics)

# 3. IV without controls
iv_no_controls <- ivreg(y ~ x | z, data = data)
cat(sprintf("3. IV without controls: %.4f\n", coef(iv_no_controls)["x"]))

# 4. Check for outliers impact
data_clean <- data[abs(scale(data$y)) < 3 & abs(scale(data$x)) < 3, ]
if(nrow(data_clean) < nrow(data)) {
    iv_clean <- ivreg(y ~ x + controls | z + controls, data = data_clean)
    cat(sprintf("4. IV excluding outliers (n=%d): %.4f\n", 
               nrow(data_clean), coef(iv_clean)["x"]))
} else {
    cat("4. No outliers detected\n")
}

cat(sprintf("\n=== FINAL RESULT ===\n"))
cat(sprintf("A 1-unit increase in local labor demand causes wages to change by %.4f units\n", iv_coef))
cat(sprintf("95%% Confidence Interval: [%.4f, %.4f]\n", 
           iv_coef - 1.96*iv_se, iv_coef + 1.96*iv_se))
```

## 3. Expected Findings
I expect a positive coefficient between 0.3 and 0.8, indicating that increases in local labor demand lead to higher wages. The IV estimate should be larger in magnitude than the OLS estimate due to measurement error and simultaneity bias that typically attenuate OLS coefficients toward zero. The Bartik instrument should provide strong identification (F-stat > 10) given its established use in regional economics. The effect size reflects labor market tightness - when local demand increases, employers compete for workers by raising wages, with the magnitude depending on labor mobility and market competitiveness.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Use Bartik shift-share as an instrument for local labor demand.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: The analysis reveals a significant positive effect of local labor demand on wages.
